# Synthetic benchmark source

This file is generated solely for the author-teaching benchmark. It is not an
external reference or empirical evidence. All scenarios and numbers below are
invented for testing whether a first draft states its assumptions and reasoning.

## 1. Dilution

A solution has concentration 20 mg/mL. A technician measures 100 mL, adds
solvent until the final volume is 500 mL, and assumes no solute is lost. Solute
amount before dilution is concentration times volume. After dilution, that same
solute amount is spread across the final volume.

## 2. Feedback

A small greenhouse targets 24 °C. At noon its sensor reads 27 °C. A controller
compares the reading with the target and opens a vent when the measured
quantity is above target. A later reading tells the controller whether the
action moved the temperature toward the target. The vent changes temperature;
the sensor only reports it.

## 3. Association and cause

A school compares assignment completion for students who chose to receive a
weekly reminder with completion for students who did not. The reminder group
has higher completion. Students chose their own group, and motivation was not
measured. A randomized assignment of reminders would make the groups more
comparable, though the result would still apply only to the setting studied.
